subject: Custodian keystore access and cross-border consent for private deployment
messages:
From: Jane Porter <jane.porter@heliohealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: HelioHealth Legal <legal@heliohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — keystore custody and cross-border access

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for walking us through the Private deployment options yesterday. Legal had two follow-ups we need in writing before we can sign the DPA appendix:

1) Customer-controlled keys: we want confirmation that if HelioHealth uses our own KMS/keystore (on-prem or in a customer-managed cloud KMS), Redwood engineers will never have access to plaintext customer keys or to a process that would allow deriving them, except under an explicit, documented break-glass procedure that HelioHealth pre-approves.

2) Cross-border access: because some of our EU patient data will be processed in staging/backup sites, we need to understand under what operational scenarios Redwood personnel (or subprocessors) might access data or keys from outside the EU, and whether the DPA can include a clause limiting access to EU-resident personnel or approved subprocessors only.

Can you provide a short written summary of the operational constraints and proposed contract language we can pass to procurement/legal? Also attaching our internal privacy matrix for reference (see attachment).

Best,
Jane

Attachment: helio_privacy_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet; redacted)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jane Porter <jane.porter@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — keystore custody and cross-border access

Jane — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Marcus (Security) and Monica (AE) are looped to confirm operational and contract language.

- Customer-controlled keys: Redwood supports two models for Private deployments: (A) Bring-your-own-KMS (customer-managed keys) where we never possess key material and only store encrypted secrets; and (B) Customer-owned keystore with optional key-escrow for break-glass. For (A) our standard practice is that all key operations (rotate, sign, decrypt) require an HSM/KMS call in the customer environment; Redwood hosts no key plaintext. For (B) we can operate a KMS agent inside the VPC or on-prem; break-glass access requires multi-party approval, an auditable request, and can be limited to named roles.

- Cross-border access: By default we route control-plane telemetry to the region you choose; we can add contractual commitments to process data and logs within EU regions and to restrict operator consoles to EU-hosted bastions. There are two edge cases: emergency remediation (operator break-glass) and third-party subprocessor escalations. Both can be limited in the DPA to EU-resident personnel or to subprocessors that have signed EU data transfer safeguards.

I've attached a short outline of proposed language and an operations summary. Marcus — can you confirm the exact wording for a DPA appendix (break-glass checklist + operator role whitelist) and whether we can commit to EU-only operator access for Helio?

Thanks,
Lauren

Attachments: redwood_keystore_model.pdf (summary)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jane Porter <jane.porter@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — keystore custody and cross-border access

Hi all — tagging onto Lauren's note with concrete operational commitments we can include in an appendix. Below is proposed text plus an explanation of mechanisms. Please feel free to redline.

Proposed DPA appendix language (draft):
1) Key custody: Customer shall retain ownership and exclusive control of key material when using Customer-managed KMS. Redwood shall not store, export, or otherwise have access to customer key plaintext or private keying material. Any operator action that would expose key material requires documented, pre-approved break-glass approval from the named HelioHealth contacts and must be executed in-customer environment.

2) Break-glass and escrow: Where customer elects a KMS-escrow arrangement, Redwood will only access escrowed key material under a) an event logged in our incident tracker, b) a signed work-order or DocuSign approval from HelioHealth's security lead, and c) with two Redwood approvers from separate teams (security + ops). All access will be audited and reversible.

3) Cross-border access restrictions: Redwood will ensure that operator consoles and remediation tooling for HelioHealth private deployments are hosted in the EU region selected by HelioHealth. Redwood further agrees that operator accounts authorized for HelioHealth will be held to an EU-resident operator policy and that any exception (e.g., an on-call engineer based outside the EU) will require prior written approval from HelioHealth and will be explicitly logged.

4) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a list of subprocessors that may process HelioHealth data. Any subprocessors that would transfer data outside the EU will only be engaged after HelioHealth's explicit consent; transfers will be governed by standard SCCs or equivalent safeguards.

Mechanics/notes:
- Technical enforcement is via VPC-hosted agents and customer-side KMS calls; we can deploy a minimal agent inside your VPC so key operations never leave the boundary.
- For observability, we can redact any sensitive token-level logs and provide a telemetry-only stream that excludes request payloads unless you opt-in for deeper tracing for debugging.

Attachments: redwood_keystore_model.pdf (detailed), helio_privacy_matrix.xlsx (for reference)

Happy to iterate on precise language.

— Marcus
Security Engineering
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jane Porter <jane.porter@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — keystore custody and cross-border access

Jane — quick commercial note: Helio has asked for EU-only operator access and the escrow break-glass guardrails. Both are feasible. From a contracting standpoint our Legal team prefers to include the proposed appendix language Marcus drafted and then accept Helio's redlines.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus to provide final appendix draft (we'll version as App A to the DPA).
- Lauren to confirm whether Helio wants an agent-only model (recommended) or KMS-escrow.
- Helio legal to provide any required redline by EOD Monday so we can turn around a DocuSign.

I'll prep a one-page summary for procurement and loop our Legal as needed.

Thanks,
Monica
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Jane Porter <jane.porter@heliohealth.com>

Date: Sat, 11 Aug 2028 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — keystore custody and cross-border access

Monica / Lauren / Marcus — thanks for the rapid responses and the draft language. HelioHealth legal reviewed the appendix and proposed two small redlines (1. require explicit retention period for operator audit logs; 2. clarify that exceptions to EU-only operator access are timeboxed to a maximum of 72 hours unless otherwise approved). We can accept the agent model (preferred) and will sign the appendix once these redlines are incorporated.

Please send revised App A (DPA appendix) and a DocuSign link and we'll route to our CISO for signature.

Jane
